name: successful deposits and withdrawals append account-local statements
input: one account with an opening balance, one deposit, and one withdrawal
test:
ledger = BankLedger()
ledger.open_account('maya', 10)
assert ledger.deposit('maya', 5, 'refund') == 'entry-1'
assert ledger.withdraw('maya', 4, 'lunch') == 'entry-2'
assert ledger.balance('maya') == 11
assert ledger.statement('maya') == [
    {'id': 'entry-1', 'type': 'deposit', 'amount': 5, 'balance_after': 15, 'memo': 'refund'},
    {'id': 'entry-2', 'type': 'withdraw', 'amount': 4, 'balance_after': 11, 'memo': 'lunch'},
]

name: accounts stay independent while entry identifiers remain global
input: two accounts each receive a different mutation
test:
ledger = BankLedger()
ledger.open_account('a')
ledger.open_account('b', 3)
assert ledger.deposit('a', 7) == 'entry-1'
assert ledger.withdraw('b', 1) == 'entry-2'
assert ledger.balance('a') == 7
assert ledger.balance('b') == 2
assert [row['id'] for row in ledger.statement('a')] == ['entry-1']
assert [row['id'] for row in ledger.statement('b')] == ['entry-2']

name: overdrafts are atomic and do not consume an entry identifier
input: an account with three credits followed by an oversized withdrawal
test:
ledger = BankLedger()
ledger.open_account('a', 3)
try:
    ledger.withdraw('a', 4, 'too much')
    raise AssertionError('expected InsufficientFundsError')
except InsufficientFundsError:
    pass
assert ledger.balance('a') == 3
assert ledger.statement('a') == []
assert ledger.deposit('a', 1) == 'entry-1'
